knowledge_graph.title: Blood pressure
knowledge_graph.description: Blood pressure is the pressure of circulating blood against the walls of blood vessels. Most of this pressure results from the heart pumping blood through the circulatory system. When used without qualification, the term "blood pressure" refers to the pressure in a brachial artery, where it is most commonly measured.

related_questions.question: What is blood pressure in simple terms?

text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure is a measurement of the force exerted by blood on the walls of your arteries as the heart pumps it through the body. It is typically expressed as two numbers:
snippet_highlighted_words: a measurement of the force exerted by blood on the walls of your arteries as the heart pumps it through the body

list.snippet: Systolic pressure: The pressure when the heart beats and pumps blood into the arteries.
Diastolic pressure: The pressure when the heart rests between beats.

text_blocks.snippet: Normal blood pressure is considered to be less than 120/80 mmHg (millimeters of mercury). High blood pressure (hypertension) is diagnosed when blood pressure consistently exceeds 130/80 mmHg.

Blood pressure can be measured using a blood pressure cuff and a stethoscope or an electronic monitor. It is important to have your blood pressure checked regularly by a healthcare professional to monitor for any potential health risks associated with high blood pressure.
